subject: BlueHarbor Labs trial activation, schedule & risk alignment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara@blueharborlabs.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueHarbor Labs — trial activation & proposed next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the BlueHarbor team. Quick recap and my suggested next steps so we can kick off the trial cleanly: 

Summary (what we heard)
- Goal: validate a live inference flow for the customer support summarization use case at 10k sessions/month, sub-150ms 95th percentile inference for 1k-token prompts, and maintain ≤$0.45/1k token unit cost using batching/kv-cache optimizations.
- Integrations: ingest via S3 -> Redwood Private model endpoint; results back to Support DB.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm)
1) Latency: 95th ≤ 150ms on representative 1k-token traces
2) Throughput: sustained 120 qps for burst windows (15m) and steady 2k qpm
3) Quality: >0.85 F1 on your summarization eval set (we'll run the holdout)
4) Cost: unit cost ≤ $0.45/1k tokens using recommended config

Plan & timeline (draft)
- Kickoff week: Apr 20 — 4-week trial (Apr 20 -> May 17)
- Week 0 (pre-kick): data access & test keys (owner: BlueHarbor eng)
- Week 1: integration + baseline run (owner: Rafael)
- Weeks 2–3: eval runs, tuning (owner: Vivek)
- Week 4: final readout & decision

Owners
- Program owner: Marissa (Redwood) — coordination, readout
- Infra & deployment: Rafael (Redwood)
- Evaluation & metrics: Vivek (Redwood)
- BlueHarbor lead: Sara (eng)

Risks / open items
- Data residency / KMS expectations (Sara to confirm)
- Representative samples: need a 1k-record holdout set
- Network/VPC peering timing for private endpoints

Attachments: trial-scope-v1.pdf (scope + sample dataset checklist)
Related: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (outline of milestones) — see HubSpot link below.

Ask: Please confirm the success metrics above and availability for kickoff week Apr 20. If that week doesn't work we can shift. Once you confirm I'll send calendar invites and the mutual action plan for signatures.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

---
From: Sara Kim <sara@blueharborlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@blueharborlabs.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor Labs — trial activation & proposed next steps

Thanks Marissa — that all looks sensible. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Success metrics: the latency & throughput targets are what the execs want to see; we'll also include an end-user satisfaction survey (simple NPS on summaries). Can we include that as an auxiliary metric?
- KMS / retention: we prefer customer-managed KMS for keys and a 90-day retention default for logs unless otherwise agreed. I will share our security questionnaire during the day.
- Kickoff: Apr 20 works for our team for a 60-min kickoff. Would you be able to do a 30-min technical deep-dive with our infra lead prior to kickoff (Apr 18 or Apr 19)?

If you can confirm the technical dry run and the inclusion of the NPS check we'll sign off on the scope.

Sara Kim
VP Engineering, BlueHarbor Labs
sara@blueharborlabs.com

Subject: Re: BlueHarbor Labs — trial activation & proposed next steps

Thanks — replying with a concrete schedule and owner commitments so we can get invites out. Attaching the mutual-action-plan.xlsx with milestone dates.

Proposed schedule (finalized)
- Apr 18: 30-min tech dry run (Redwood infra ↔ BlueHarbor infra) — Rafael + BlueHarbor infra lead
- Apr 20 (Mon) 10:00 PT: Kickoff (60 min) — agenda: goals, data access, runbook, roles
- Weekly check-ins: Fridays 09:00 PT (15–30 min) — status, blockers, metric readout
- May 17: Final readout (45 min) + decision gate

Mutual action owners
- Rafael (Redwood): infra setup, VPC peering, endpoint provisioning — target ready by Apr 19
- Vivek (Redwood): eval harness, metric collection, and baseline runs — first baseline by Apr 23
- Marissa (Redwood): program coordination, readout deck, and final decision facilitation
- Sara / Tom (BlueHarbor): dataset delivery, access permissions, stakeholder attendance for readout

Top risks & mitigation
- Data access delay → mitigation: parallelize with a masked sample set we can use for baseline runs
- KMS mismatch → mitigation: Rafael to share supported KMS integrations and options for customer-managed keys
- Unexpected production-like traffic patterns → mitigation: synthetic load test window in Week 2

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/3412556 (deal BHL-2027-042)

If everyone is aligned I will send calendar invites for Apr 18 and Apr 20 and upload the MAP to the shared drive.

Rafael
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai

- Share the pre-kick checklist in the drive: sample dataset (1k holdout), service account for API access, and a minimal test harness.
- Draft readout deck template and circulate by Apr 24.

Pre-kick checklist (quick)
- BlueHarbor: share holdout sample (CSV/JSON), confirm KMS preference, provide test service account
- Redwood: provision test endpoint, provide test API key (scoped), produce baseline trace run

Proposed weekly agenda (15–30m)
1) Quick metrics snapshot (latency / throughput / cost)
2) Blockers & actions (2 items)
3) Next week priorities (owners)

I'll also make sure Rafael posts the KMS options doc to the shared drive so you can confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Marissa
